title: Making Good Tech Decisions: measuring cost, value and risk with ramp-up, maintenance and off-boarding curves
summary: Theo's first conference talk gives a framework for picking technology: measure cost (ramp up, maintenance, off-boarding), value, and risk against where the team and business are heading. He compares tRPC, GraphQL, Redwood and create-t3-app to show why modular choices keep the cost of leaving cheap.

principles.text: Treat tech picks like hiring: a big investment and a bet you must plan to maintain or exit.
principles.quote: just like employees tech is a big investment that you make and are to an extent betting on you have to think about the long-term impact of those decisions

principles.text: Break technology cost into ramp up, maintenance over time, and ramp off (off-boarding), since they vary wildly by tool.
principles.quote: i like to break this into three separate sections the ramp up time the maintenance overtime as well as the ramp off time

principles.text: Judge a tech's value by time saved, user wins, developer happiness and hiring impact, not just features.
principles.quote: how much time does this library save us what are the wins that our users will feel from these technologies how much happier are developers

principles.text: Treat risk separately from cost and value; assess your own tolerance for it and plan around it.
principles.quote: risk is something that we don't necessarily know but it's something we can plan around

principles.text: Pick the tool that fits the current stage and accept paying the migration cost later, when growth justifies it.
principles.quote: we have five people working on ping right now it is not that big a deal for us to make it way smoother to get those things out knowing that we can pay this cost in the future

principles.text: Choose modular tools: cheap off-boarding is the easiest way to reduce the risk of any technology bet.
principles.quote: it's also without question the easiest way to reduce the risk of any technology bet that you make
